identity.name: Ransomware Pre-Encryption Behavioral Anomaly on a Host — Cortex Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) (T1486 / T1490 / T1083)
identity.summary: A host process shows an anomalous file rewrite rate, per-file entropy spike, and snapshot/backup inhibition that deviate from the host's learned Cortex baseline — the pre-encryption fingerprint of Akira (Howling Scorpius). No single write is a known-bad IOC, so signature BIOCs miss it; the deviation plus causality chain is what an auto-tuned ABIOC fires on.
identity.description: Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) is a first-party Cortex detection type distinct from a hand-authored BIOC: PANW authors and continually tunes ABIOCs against the endpoint, user, and network behavioral profiles Cortex learns per environment, firing on a single suspicious event that carries an identified chain of causality. This scenario exercises that detector class on the ENDPOINT plane against the earliest, cheapest-to-catch phase of a ransomware intrusion — the moment BEFORE bulk encryption completes and while recovery is being inhibited. It models the tradecraft attributed to Howling Scorpius (the Akira ransomware operation), whose Linux/ESXi encryptors enumerate a target file set, rewrite files at a rate and entropy no legitimate workload produces, and delete snapshots/backups so victims cannot roll back. Cortex has learned this host's normal file-I/O profile: a small, stable set of processes writing at a modest, low-entropy cadence (log rotation, package updates, scheduled tar/rsync jobs) and a backup routine that CREATES snapshots on a schedule, never bulk-DELETES them. The scenario injects two behavioral deviations from that learned baseline: (a) a single process producing a rapid burst of high-entropy file writes/renames with a uniform new extension at a rate far above the host's learned file-modification profile, and (b) a recovery-inhibition burst that deletes snapshot/backup artefacts a routine backup job never removes. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on a specific encryptor hash, ransom-note string, or known extension would miss a fresh Akira build — which is exactly the point: the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on the deviation from the host's learned behavior and anchors it to the causality chain (file enumeration -> high-entropy mass rewrite -> snapshot/backup deletion). Two ABIOCs cover the two deviation shapes; supporting validation XQL confirms the learned file-I/O baseline and surfaces the pre-encryption burst; a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into a single pre-encryption-ransomware incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex's behavioral analytics caught a novel encryptor no static signature was written for. Fully SAFE-MODE: writes land only in an isolated /tmp victim directory, nothing outside it is touched, and cleanup restores the directory.

campaigns: Akira ransomware double-extortion intrusions against enterprise Linux/ESXi and Windows estates (2023-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-011 — Ransomware pre-encryption behavioral deviation on a learned host file-I/O baseline for Cortex ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM Linux agent installed on the target host so per-process file-I/O and command telemetry reaches xdr_data.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the host produced only its normal file-I/O (log rotation, package updates, scheduled tar/rsync) so Cortex learned the endpoint file-modification profile.

payload.code:
# No known-bad payloads, no real encryption. Reproduce the pre-encryption
# telemetry shape: enumerate an isolated victim set, rewrite it at a high
# rate with high-entropy content and a uniform new extension, then inhibit
# recovery by deleting snapshot/backup artefacts. All writes stay in /tmp.
set -euo pipefail
VDIR=/tmp/cortexsim_preenc; mkdir -p $VDIR
for i in $(seq 1 60); do echo baseline-content-$i > $VDIR/doc_$i.dat; done
find $VDIR -type f > /tmp/cortexsim_preenc_targets.txt
while read -r f; do head -c 4096 /dev/urandom > $f.locked && rm -f $f; done < /tmp/cortexsim_preenc_targets.txt
rm -f /tmp/cortexsim_snapshot_baseline.img /tmp/cortexsim_backup_baseline.tar 2>/dev/null || true

input_variables.name: VICTIM_FILE_COUNT
input_variables.description: Number of isolated victim files seeded then rewritten to produce the high-rate, high-entropy pre-encryption burst.

expected_artifacts.description: A single process producing a rapid burst of high-entropy file rewrites with a uniform new extension at a rate above the host's learned file-modification baseline.
A recovery-inhibition process deleting snapshot/backup artefacts a routine backup job never removes.

abiocs.name: EDR-011 Anomalous Pre-Encryption File-Modification Burst Deviating from Host Baseline
abiocs.description: A single process produces a rapid burst of high-entropy file writes/renames with a uniform new extension at a rate far above the host's learned file-modification profile. Every write uses legitimate syscalls and the encryptor may be a fresh, unhashed Akira build, so a signature BIOC misses it; the ABIOC fires on the rate-and-entropy deviation from the learned endpoint baseline, anchored to the enumeration-then-mass-rewrite causality chain rather than any known-bad extension or hash.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME)
| filter actor_process_image_name not in ("tar", "gzip", "rsync", "dpkg", "apt", "logrotate")
| comp count() as file_ops, count_distinct(action_file_extension) as ext_spread by agent_hostname, actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_image_name
| filter file_ops >= 200
| sort desc file_ops
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, file_ops, ext_spread
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned host file-I/O baseline (few processes, modest low-entropy cadence) -> file enumeration -> single-process high-entropy mass rewrite whose rate exceeds the learned profile, anchored to the enumerating process lineage.

abiocs.name: EDR-011 Recovery-Inhibition Snapshot Deletion Deviating from Host Baseline
abiocs.description: A process deletes snapshot/backup artefacts on a host whose learned backup routine only CREATES snapshots on a schedule and never bulk-deletes them. The deletion co-occurs with the high-entropy file-modification burst. The ABIOC fires on the recovery-inhibition deviation from the host's learned backup behavior, anchored to the mass-rewrite that immediately precedes it.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("rm", "shred", "btrfs", "lvremove", "vgremove", "unlink")
| filter action_process_command_line contains "snapshot" or action_process_command_line contains "backup" or action_process_command_line contains ".img"
| comp count() as recovery_inhibit_ops by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
| filter recovery_inhibit_ops >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, recovery_inhibit_ops
abiocs.causality_anchor: High-entropy mass-rewrite burst on the host -> deletion of snapshot/backup artefacts the learned backup routine never removes, anchored to the co-occurring encryptor process.

xql_queries.name: EDR-011 Host File-Modification Baseline Learned
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| comp count() as file_ops by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter file_ops >= 1
| sort desc file_ops
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, file_ops

xql_queries.name: EDR-011 Pre-Encryption File Burst Surfaced on Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME)
| comp count() as burst_ops by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter burst_ops >= 50
| sort desc burst_ops
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, burst_ops

correlation_rules.name: Pre-Encryption Ransomware on Host — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(EDR-011 Anomalous Pre-Encryption File-Modification Burst Deviating from Host Baseline) AND ABIOC(EDR-011 Recovery-Inhibition Snapshot Deletion Deviating from Host Baseline) — fuses the two auto-tuned behavioral deviations on the same host into a single pre-encryption-ransomware incident anchored to the enumeration -> mass-rewrite -> recovery-inhibition causality chain, catching the Akira encryptor before bulk encryption completes.

analytics_modules: Cortex XSIAM Analytics — auto-tuned behavioral profiling of per-endpoint file-I/O rate, write entropy, and backup/recovery behavior

products.evidence_query: Two ABIOCs fire on the host file-I/O behavioral deviation; CR-EDR-0011 stitches them into one pre-encryption-ransomware incident anchored to the enumeration -> mass-rewrite -> recovery-inhibition causality chain.

use_cases.name: Ransomware Pre-Encryption Behavioral Anomaly Detection via Cortex ABIOC
use_cases.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn a host's normal file-I/O and backup profile and detect the pre-encryption phase of a ransomware intrusion — a single process rewriting files at anomalous rate and entropy while deleting snapshots — anchored to its causality chain, where no static signature was written for a fresh encryptor build.

test_cases.objective: Cortex learns the host file-I/O baseline and an injected pre-encryption burst plus recovery inhibition fires both ABIOCs.
preconditions: EDR target with the Cortex Linux agent installed.
Baseline window elapsed with the host producing only normal file-I/O.
steps: Let the file-I/O baseline window elapse.
Seed an isolated victim set, run a high-entropy mass rewrite, and delete snapshot/backup artefacts.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-EDR-0011 raise a pre-encryption-ransomware incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `EDR-011 Anomalous Pre-Encryption File-Modification Burst Deviating from Host Baseline` fires.
ABIOC `EDR-011 Recovery-Inhibition Snapshot Deletion Deviating from Host Baseline` fires.
Correlation CR-EDR-0011 raises one stitched pre-encryption-ransomware incident.

preventive_controls: Enforce immutable/offline backups and snapshot retention locks so recovery cannot be inhibited by a compromised host, turning a T1490 attempt into a non-event.
Restrict which accounts and processes may delete snapshot/backup artefacts; require change control for bulk snapshot removal.
Deploy canary files whose modification triggers immediate isolation so a mass-rewrite is contained before it spreads.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-endpoint file-I/O rate and write-entropy baseline rather than hand-authoring static rules for individual encryptor hashes or extensions.
Alert on a single process whose file-modification rate or write entropy exceeds the host's learned baseline.
Alert on snapshot/backup deletion co-occurring with an anomalous file-modification burst.
